**Finding submitted: deviation (high severity, restrictive covenants).**

- **Deviation found at § 7.2 (p0026):** "Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives." This right-of-first-refusal precondition functions as de facto exclusivity on us, and it directly contradicts § 12.3, where Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no exclusivity or most-favoured-customer commitment. The § 2.1 three-year take-or-pay minimum reinforces the lock-in (flagged for the minimum-commitment rule rather than redlined here).
- **Redline (preferred, validated ok:true):** delete § 7.2 in full, with the fallback (defined category, ≤12 months, automatic exit on Vendor performance failure) offered in the comment.
- **Not flagged:** non-exclusive licence grants, exclusive-remedy/jurisdiction language, and Vendor-side exclusivity — none restrict our supplier freedom.
